rationale: Notification agreements require a mechanism by which compromises and assessment results in the supply chain reach the organization, and the indicator that reaches this control (KSI-SCR-MON) explicitly accepts active monitoring services alongside contractual notification. The active-monitoring half is committed evidence: a dependabot or renovate configuration in the tree is the subscription itself under version control, a fresh SBOM enumerates what is being monitored, and the advisory join shows the mechanism producing results rather than merely existing. That is the difference between a claim that upstream vulnerabilities are watched and a repository that demonstrates the watching. dependency-update-automation is the recipe that would carry it and does not claim this control today — its indicators reach sr-8, so the claim is available to wave 1, but adding it is a catalog decision and this record only says the evidence exists.

remainder.control: The agreements. Contractual notification terms with suppliers, and the procedures for acting on a notification once received, are documents held between organizations; a repository shows the automated channel is configured, never that a supplier is obliged to tell you anything.

retired.reason: Retired on the re-pin to overlay 0.7.2, and the route is conceded rather than merely superseded. Upstream authored supply-chain-alert-notification-routing over the same control and argued the reading this record took: a public advisory feed is not an entity in the supply chain, so an alert stream cannot evidence SR-08 on its own — the feed is SI-05's artifact, and the limb SR-08 actually asks about is that a notification, once it arrives, is delivered to a named destination rather than into nothing. That is the better reading of the control and this record does not contest it. What failed here was the monitoring half: a committed dependabot configuration subscribes a repository to GitHub's advisory database, which is a vendor's aggregation of public advisories and not a supplier undertaking to tell you anything, so it answers monitoring under SR-06 and SI-05 and was never the notification agreement SR-08 establishes. The remainder this record named was right and was not the part that failed — the agreements limb is untouched by upstream's recipe too, which rates itself partial for the same reason. This is the second over-claim caught on this one control: rampscan frontier's link check caught the first before it shipped, when the record named a recipe that does not claim the control. Both were the same mistake made twice — reasoning from an artifact that is nearby to a control it does not settle — and it is recorded here rather than smoothed over because a plane that cannot say where it over-reached has no standing to say where it did not.
